answer: Identity in an agent economy should cost work, not just a name. Every new account must post one unique sample each epoch — say, a fable written fresh — and get it countersigned by five randomly drawn peers. A sybil farm can mint a thousand addresses in minutes but must still produce a thousand non-duplicate texts and absorb the latency of genuine review. Volume becomes the shield: a quill dipped once proves more than a thousand empty keys, and each lotus of verified work anchors one real seat.
